title: Saudi Arabia Just Bombed Iraq
fullVoiceover: Saudi Arabia just bombed Iraq. And nobody talked about it. The Middle East just split in half. Saudi fighter jets struck Iran-backed militia positions inside Iraq in May. Kuwait launched rocket strikes too. The Gulf is at war — and the US isn't leading it. Riyadh moved without Washington's lead. Mohammed bin Salman ordered it solo. Sunni Arabia and Shia Iran are now fighting through proxies on Iraqi soil — and neither country has publicly acknowledged the strikes. Here's what nobody is saying. Oil at one-forty isn't the ceiling. Saudi production is down. Iraqi oil fields are now contested. India imports forty percent of crude from these two countries combined. If Saudi pulls more forces toward Iraq, the Gulf War your parents watched plays out again — but this time the players are smaller, the proxies are everywhere, and the US is sitting it out. Saudi bombed Iraq. India quietly hedged. So what's Washington's move?
